Thanks for the context, Soojin. I reviewed the summary and the draft. A few immediate notes:

- Per our handbook, the standard support plan timeline is 60 days for an individual contributor at Ethan's level; please change the 30-day references in your draft to 60 days unless you have a compelling, documented reason for a shorter window.
- Please attach copies of the prior coaching notes and the last three 1:1 summaries (I see you referenced the manager log; we need PDFs for the file).
- I'll attach the HR canonical template for the support plan — it has the necessary acknowledgment and appeal language we track. (see pip_template_hr_v2.docx)

I also recommend we schedule a calibration call with People Ops so we have a uniform approach across any concurrent performance conversations.

I'll review again once you update the timeline and add the evidence.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Manager, People Operations
Redwood Inference

On Thu, Apr 22, 2027 at 10:22 AM Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks for the context, Soojin...

I reviewed the draft and have a few redlines (see attached redlines_legal.pdf). High level:

- Remove any language that suggests "termination is likely" during the plan period. PIPs must be framed as a remediation/support mechanism; if there is a separate disciplinary track, that should be documented elsewhere.
- Replace "will result in termination" with "may result in further action up to and including termination" and only if backed by explicit documented steps.
- Neutralize subjective language ("poor attitude", "unwilling") and replace with specific examples and dates.
- Add one sentence that confirms accommodations (if applicable) and directs the manager to coordinate with People Ops before any change to schedule or role.

I'll loop counsel on the specific wording for any non-standard clauses — cc'd above. Once Soojin updates with the 60-day timeline and the manager evidence, I can provide a final sign-off.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
General Counsel (acting)
Redwood Inference
